newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.

text.p: COSTELLO UNAMUSED BY COMMONWEALTH BANK AD
Federal Treasurer, Peter Costello, says the Commonwealth Bank would be better off spending its money giving borrowers a better deal, rather than taking out advertisements.
He was commenting on an advertisement for the bank's no-frills six-point-seven per cent home loan, which says: "If you really want to save on a home loan Mr Costello, we'll tell you where to go."
But Mr Costello told Melbourne radio station 3-A-W this loan is restricted, and isn't linked to the standard variable mortgage rate.
The Treasurer has again urged the Commonwealth, the National Australia Bank and Westpac to follow the A-N-Z Bank's lead, and pass on the full cut in official rates to their customers.
LOIS SAYS SADDENED AND EXHILARATED BY CONVENTION
The former Chair of the Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Commission says the Australian Reconciliation Convention has saddened but exhilarated her.
The Covention in Melbourne concludes today.
Lois O'Donohue said she's disappointed political leaders haven't made a consentual agreement to reconciliation, but the high spirits of Aboriginal delegates has given her heart.
Ms O'Donohue says from now on, indigenous people must face the politics of reconciliation.
She says it's not just about overcoming disadvantages, nor simply a case of saying "I'm sorry" or "we forgive", but that those words are essential starting points without qualification. - - - -
TRADITIONAL JABILUKA OWNERS REJECT ERA MONEY
The traditional owners of the proposed Jabiluka uranium mine site in the Northern Territory have decided to reject their royalty payments for the mining lease.
Spokesperson Jacqui Katona says members of the Jabiluku Association have decided to give back the royalties paid by mining company ERA, because they don't want the mine.
She says the beneficiaries of the royalty have instructed the Northern Land Council not to accept or distribute any money from ERA.
CHARGES AGAINST WOODS ADJOURNED
In the ACT Magistrates court charges of defrauding the Commonwealth due to be heard today against former Liberal Senator Bob Woods have again been adjourned.
This morning before Magistrate John Burns the Commonwealth Prosecutor Grant Lawlor handed over to the court a number of diaries belonging to Mr Woods' former lover Roxanne Cameron.
Phillip Gibson, acting for Mr Woods, said he would be arguing for access to the diaries when the matter resumed on July first.
Mr Gibson said he'd also issued subpoennas for access to interviews by Channel Nine's Sixty Minutes program with Miss Cameron.
Magistrate John Burns said he would require Mr Woods to enter a plea during the next sitting.
WOOLDRIDGE: AUSTRALIANS NOT READY TO SAY SORRY
Federal Health Minister, Michael Wooldridge, has indicated there's movement towards an apology to indigenous Australians from the Federal Parliament, but says it needs to come from the heart.
However, Dr Wooldridge says Australia isn't yet ready to say sorry to Aborigines forcibly removed from their families.
He says most Australians don't understand what Aboriginal people have been through.
Dr Wooldridge says in his experience, the bitterness most Aboriginal people fear stems from events that occurred during their own lifetimes, rather than those further back in history.
TV CRIME CATCHERS CLAIM ANOTHER SCALP
A man who appeared on the television crime show, "Australia's Most Wanted", on Monday night has been arrested on the New South Wales Central Coast.
Fifty-seven-year-old Dennis Claude Pearson is wanted on a number of indecent assault charges in Melbourne, and was arrested in a house at Ettalong, yesterday.
He has appeared in Woy Woy Court, and will remain in custody until his next court appearance on June 10th .
Plans are underway to extradite Mr Pearson to Melbourne.
TUCKEY SLAMS GG FOR APOLOGY TO INDIGENOUS AUSTRALIANS
Federal Liberal MP, Wilson Tuckey, says the Governor-General was wrong to apologise to Aborigines forcibly removed from their parents.

Sir William Deane yesterday told the Australian Reconciliation Convention in Melbourne he was profoundly sorry for policies which oppressed indigenous Australians in the past. Sir William said the appalling state of Aboriginal health, unemployment and living conditions today is due to the oppression of the past.
But Mr Tuckey, who says the Reconciliation Convention is a waste of money, says the fact that Sir William gives his advice for free is a measure of its value.
VICTORIAN GOVERNMENT TACKLES FOOD ESSENCE
The Victorian Government is amending liquor regulations to ban certain quantities of food essence to combat under-age drinking.
Small Business Minister, Louise Asher, has called for the removal of large bottles of food essence from general sale.
She says police have been concerned about minors buying 375-millilitre essence bottles which register up to 86 per cent alcohol by volume.
Ms Asher says the new Liquor Control Regulations will prevent young people buying the large bottles from supermarket shelves.
